channel.title: mvGPT | Minimum Viable GPT: A Language Model from Scratch
channel.description: Understand language models from the ground up: the whole training pipeline, from pretraining to reinforcement learning, with evaluation, metrics and diagnostics.

item.title: Episode 28: Attention heads in our GPT, seen and tested
item.description: We look inside our agent while it copies a name into a query, with each head's attention written out, the logit lens, and a page of our own, then turn the heads that look at the name off to see what they do.

item.title: Episode 27: Speculative decoding from scratch
item.description: A draft guesses the next few tokens, and our agent checks them in the pass that writes its own, so it writes what greedy decoding writes in fewer passes. Two drafts, prompt lookup and a small model trained for thirty minutes, measured on the agent's tasks.

item.title: Episode 26: Constrained decoding: structured LLM output
item.description: Nothing is trained. Before each token inside a query's name, our agent's graph role masks the tokens that would take the name off a list, and we measure two lists, the graph's names and the task's words.

item.title: Episode 25: AI agent: a graph database and a calculator
item.description: Our agent gets a fourth role, which queries smollerGraph in Cypher, so it can take two facts from a graph database and combine them with the calculator, and we measure what it kept of its old tasks.

item.title: Episode 24: Text to Cypher: our GPT asks a graph database
item.description: We fine-tune our agent to write Cypher queries for smollerGraph, the graph database built in our sibling series, and to answer from what comes back, then measure it with the graph and without.

item.title: Episode 23: Muon vs AdamW, Lion and Sophia: a fair race
item.description: We write AdamW from scratch, then race it against Lion, Sophia and Muon on our stories model, each with its own sweep of the learning rate, and measure the steps, the time and the memory each needs.

item.title: Episode 22: Long context LLM: stretching RoPE with YaRN
item.description: We stretch the rotary embeddings of our web model to read four times its window, four ways and then with fifteen minutes of fine-tuning, and measure the loss by position and a pass key hidden in filler.

item.title: Episode 21: AI agent from scratch, with subagents
item.description: We fine-tune our web model into an agent that writes files and hands work to subagents, each a fresh context of the same model, and measure what the subagents buy.

item.title: Episode 20: LLM tool calling from scratch: a calculator
item.description: We fine-tune the model we pretrained on the web to call a calculator, in plain text, and measure how often it calls it right, on questions asked the way training asks and in new ways, with the calculator and without it.

item.title: Episode 19: Pretraining on the web: a GPT overnight
item.description: We pretrain a model in GPT-2 small's shape on educational web pages for a whole night, on one RTX 4090 rented for under four dollars, and measure it against GPT-2 small on HellaSwag.

item.title: Episode 18: Grouped-query attention: a smaller KV cache
item.description: We give our model grouped-query attention, where the query heads share their keys and values in groups, so the KV cache keeps fewer heads, and we check it against the attention we had and work out what it saves.

item.title: Episode 17: RMSNorm, SwiGLU, QK-norm: a modern GPT block
item.description: We bring our GPT's transformer block up to date with RMSNorm, SwiGLU, QK-norm and no biases, the changes recent open models made to it, each behind a config flag, with tests, and work out what they do to the parameter count.

item.title: Episode 16: GRPO: reinforcement learning without a critic
item.description: Our model writes eight stories per instruction, and each is scored against the others, in place of PPO's critic, with group relative policy optimisation, the reinforcement learning behind DeepSeek-R1.

item.title: Episode 15: Text diffusion: a GPT that writes all at once
item.description: We turn our GPT into a masked diffusion model, which writes a story by unhiding it, train it on the laptop and on four rented GPUs, start one from our next-token models' weights, and measure it against next-token prediction, comparing our code with LLaDA's, which trains this recipe at 8 billion parameters.

item.title: Episode 14: Batching: serving a GPT to many users at once
item.description: We serve the model as an API in the shape of OpenAI's completions, measure it against a crowd of players from a game, write the stories for the requests that arrive together as a batch, and run it in Docker, with vLLM as the alternative.

item.title: Episode 13: Flash attention from scratch: PyTorch, Triton
item.description: We write attention without its table of scores, first in PyTorch on the Mac, then as a Triton kernel on a rented NVIDIA GPU, forwards and backwards, and measure it against the FlashAttention-2 inside PyTorch.

item.title: Episode 12: Distributed training in PyTorch: 4 GPUs, DDP
item.description: We pretrain a model about six times bigger, in GPT-2 small's shape, on four RTX 4090s rented by the hour, with PyTorch's DistributedDataParallel, and measure how the speed scales from one GPU to four, and how much better the model gets in thirty minutes.

item.title: Episode 11: BPE in C++: a byte-level tokenizer for a GPT
item.description: We write a byte-level BPE tokenizer in C++, test it against a Python reference, pretrain our model on the stories in BPE, and compare the two tokenizers' models in bits per character.

item.title: Episode 10: RoPE: rotary position embeddings from scratch
item.description: We replace our model's table of positions with rotary position embeddings, which turn each query and key by its position, so attention scores depend on how far apart two tokens are, and the KV cache can slide past the context window.

item.title: Episode 9: LoRA: fine-tuning a GPT with 2% of its weights
item.description: We fine-tune our model on instructions again with LoRA, which freezes its weights and trains a small low-rank update beside them, and measure what it saves and what it learns against full fine-tuning.

item.title: Episode 8: PPO: reinforcement learning for a GPT
item.description: Our model learns from its own stories, scored as it writes them, with proximal policy optimisation, a critic and a penalty for drifting, and we measure it next to DPO.

item.title: Episode 7: DPO: teaching a GPT from preferences
item.description: With direct preference optimisation, our fine-tuned model learns from pairs of its own stories, where the one that uses more of the words asked for is preferred, and we measure what it gains and what it costs.

item.title: Episode 6: Profiling a GPT with PyTorch's profiler
item.description: We look at our model as a graph of operations in Model Explorer, profile it with PyTorch's profiler, and measure how decisions in its code change its speed on a CPU and a GPU.

item.title: Episode 5: Deploy a GPT: Hugging Face, Gradio, a browser
item.description: We save our model as a GPT-2 and push it to the Hugging Face Hub, with a tag per episode, serve it from a Gradio app on a VPS, and run it in the browser with Transformers.js.

item.title: Episode 4: KV cache from scratch in PyTorch
item.description: We add a KV cache to our model, so it runs each new token on its own and not the whole story again, and we check and time it on the CPU and the GPU.

item.title: Episode 3: SFT: fine-tuning a GPT to follow instructions
item.description: Our pretrained model learns to write the story an instruction asks for, with a loss on the story alone, and we measure how much better it follows instructions.

item.title: Episode 2: Pretraining a GPT from scratch in PyTorch
item.description: From random tokens to short stories in a first training run on a laptop, with a tokenizer, the next-token objective, a training loop and evaluation written from scratch.

item.title: Episode 1: Build a GPT from scratch in PyTorch
item.description: A small GPT written from scratch in PyTorch, from its parameters to how a prompt flows through it to the next token.
